entry.title: Toileting without a race
entry.summary: Davies describes learning to use the toilet as gradual and led by readiness, without a set age or forcing. She includes a doctor’s check when a medical issue is suspected.
entry.cue: Your child may pull at a wet or soiled diaper, seek privacy while pooping, or tell you they have peed or pooped.
detail: Davies includes these observations among possible signs of readiness, without setting a deadline. Managing clothes is one of the smaller skills the book describes along the way.

Davies prepares familiar places for clean and soiled clothes and uses matter-of-fact language when a child is wet. Her offers of the potty remain qualified by not interrupting absorbed play and not forcing the child to use it.
The source also discusses overnight changes and stool withholding. Those passages are separate from readiness; she says to check with a doctor if a medical issue is suspected.

references.locator: Complete gradual-learning unit, signs instead of ages, setup, no-force/refusal and medical qualification

ageContext.bookAge: The book gives readiness signs rather than a toilet-learning age.
ageContext.readiness: Your child may pull at a wet or soiled diaper, seek privacy while pooping, or tell you they have peed or pooped.
ageContext.note: This age band does not mean your child should be using the toilet.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
